verdict: TE Connectivity closed its fiscal year with record sales of $5.3B, up 12%, and EPS up 39% to $3.10, as AI data-center demand drove its Industrial business up 20%.

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP)
kpis.note: from continuing operations, vs $2.23 a year ago

kpis.label: Industrial Solutions sales
kpis.note: +20% vs a year ago, on AI data-center demand

kpis.label: Free cash flow
kpis.note: $1,241M — operating cash flow of $1,528M minus $287M of net capital spending (money spent on buildings and equipment)

segments.name: Transportation Solutions
segments.note: Connectors and sensors for cars, trucks and other vehicles — sales rose 7.7% to a record level as electric and data-heavy vehicles need more connections.

segments.name: Industrial Solutions
segments.note: Connectors for factories, energy and data centers — sales jumped 19.8%, powered by AI data-center demand from inside the rack out to the power grid.

segments.name: Tariff refunds to be returned
segments.note: A reconciling item, not a business: $87M of IEEPA tariff refunds TE received in fiscal 2026 that it expects to hand back to customers, so it is deducted from sales.

opex.name: SG&A
opex.note: Selling, general and administrative costs — up 4.9% as the business grew.

opex.name: R&D
opex.note: Research, development and engineering on new connectors and sensors — up 10%.

opex.name: Acquisition & integration
opex.note: Costs of buying and integrating smaller businesses.

opex.name: Restructuring
opex.note: Restructuring and other charges, net — severance and footprint changes.

takeaways.title: AI demand powers Industrial
takeaways.text: Industrial Solutions sales rose 19.8% to $2,799M — now the larger segment — as customers building AI data centers bought more power and data connectivity, from inside the rack to the energy grid.

takeaways.title: Orders point to more growth
takeaways.text: Orders hit $6.1B in the quarter, up 29% year over year, and TE guides for mid-teens sales growth and over 20% EPS growth in the first quarter of fiscal 2027.

takeaways.title: Tariff refunds will go back to customers
takeaways.text: Reported sales are after an $87M deduction for IEEPA tariff refunds TE received during fiscal 2026 that it expects to return to customers — a one-off reconciling item, not lost business.

oneTimers: $87M of IEEPA tariff refunds received in fiscal 2026, deducted from sales as a reconciling item because TE expects to return them to customers.
$14M of restructuring charges and $12M of acquisition and integration costs inside operating expenses.
otherDetail: Other income of -$17M is $23M of interest income, minus $31M of interest expense and $9M of other expense, net.
footerNote: This page models continuing operations: income from continuing operations was $901M, and after a $1M loss from discontinued operations, total net income was $900M (diluted EPS $3.09 on that basis, $3.10 from continuing operations). TE's fiscal year ends in late September, so this closes fiscal 2026 — full-year sales were a record $19.9B.
